events.title: The birth of St. Catherine of Siena
events.shortBlurb: The Dominican mystic who would counsel popes and help return the papacy to Rome was born, by tradition, on the feast of the Annunciation…
body: St. Catherine of Siena was born, according to tradition, on 25 March 1347, the feast of the Annunciation, the daughter of a Sienese dyer and one of the youngest of a very large family. From childhood she was given to prayer, and as a young Dominican tertiary she devoted herself to the sick and the poor of Siena.

Though she wrote with difficulty, her letters and her “Dialogue” made her one of the great voices of the fourteenth-century Church. She worked for peace among the Italian cities and urged Pope Gregory XI to bring the papacy back from Avignon to Rome. She was canonized in 1461 and, in 1970, declared a Doctor of the Church.

events.title: The consecration of the Florence Cathedral
events.shortBlurb: Pope Eugene IV consecrated Santa Maria del Fiore as Brunelleschi's great dome, the largest since antiquity, was completed…
body: On 25 March 1436, the feast of the Annunciation and the Florentine new year, Pope Eugene IV solemnly consecrated the cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore in Florence. The occasion marked the completion of the vast dome raised by Filippo Brunelleschi — the largest masonry dome built since antiquity, and still the largest of its kind.

For the dedication the composer Guillaume Dufay wrote the motet “Nuper rosarum flores,” whose musical proportions were said to echo those of the church. The cathedral and its dome became an enduring emblem of the union of faith and art at the dawn of the Renaissance.
